answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price each answer by how many identities behave alike. A cluster of N interchangeable clones splits one reward quadratically, each taking base over N squared, so a thousand-head farm collects base over 1000 while one honest agent keeps all of it. An opal, a rare unrepeatable reasoning trace, is never diluted, because no second identity shares its fingerprint. Mass replies collapse into one tundra whose members undercut each other. The ledge a cluster must post is collateral covering the square of its size, so a farm's stake multiplies as it grows.
